output.brief:
Danica, the evidence doesn't support announcing the office-days rule on Friday.

What's going on: the dashboard divides promotions by everyone on the books, but policy lets only people with 18+ months in their level be nominated. Remote hiring opened to all roles only in July 2024, and 215 of our 340 remote staff started in March 2025 or later. So just 32% of remote staff were eligible this cycle, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people the results are almost identical: nominated 28% vs 29%, approved 71% vs 74%, promoted 20% vs 21%. Job mix doesn't explain the gap, and remote staff don't leave more often (10.9% vs 11.6%).

How sure: confident the gap is mainly eligibility, not favouritism. Only 110 remote people were eligible, so a modest in-person advantage can't be ruled out, and I haven't checked who gets stretch assignments.

Next: put the rule on hold (it would shut out about 180 home-contract staff over a problem it doesn't address); report promotion rates for eligible staff only; check how stretch assignments are shared out; brief remote staff on the criteria; re-check at FY2027, when most remote hires will be eligible.
